Move the pointer from the link into the card and it stays open, so links and buttons inside can be clicked. The path between them is forgiving, so a diagonal move doesn’t close it.
Nothing opens on touch screens, where there is no hover. A tap follows the link, which is why the destination has to hold the same information.

One card serves many links. Create a handle with `createHoverCardHandle`, give each trigger a `payload`, and read it in the card. Moving between names glides the card to the new link instead of closing and reopening it. The old content slides out the way you moved, the new content slides in, and the height eases between the two.

`arrow` adds a pointer that joins the card's border without a seam. The side offset grows to make room for it, and it follows the card when it flips.

`delay` and `closeDelay` on the trigger set how long the pointer must rest before the card opens and how long it lingers after leaving. The 600ms default stops cards from flashing open as the pointer crosses a page.
